area.title: Layout, navigation, sign-in and shared page chrome
area.scope: What every page shares: the GOV.UK header, service name, service navigation and its items, phase banner and feedback link, footer, page title pattern, section captions, back links, error summary and shared error messages, error pages, the prototype index and version cards, sign-in, organisation choice, sign-out and sessions across services, security headers, and the accessibility and security suites. Stops at the journey's step order and scope rules (journey-flow).

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. The prototype decides look and feel only (content, wording, layout, components, question order); it never decides architecture (sets, journeys, services, URL paths, field names, data-model shape, code structure). Germinal products is a sibling set of live-animals in the animals frontend. Reference lists never wait on MDM integration; address search waits on the address lookup becoming a real feature.

claims.statement: An unauthenticated user who opens the animals notification dashboard (/live-animals) is redirected to the frontend's sign-in route, which carries the requested path as a redirect parameter.

claims.statement: Each service keeps its session in its own cookie on the shared host, so the three do not overwrite each other: sid (animals), ins-sid and ins-session (INS), plants-sid (plants), plus the identity stub's trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session; all are HttpOnly, the -sid cookies SameSite Strict and the session cookies SameSite Lax.
claims.quote: crumb, sid, ins-sid, ins-session, trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session, plants-sid, session
claims.note: Which service owns the plain 'session' cookie is not shown.

claims.statement: After a failed sign-in the stub's browser title stays 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK' with no 'Error: ' prefix, unlike the animals frontend's own error pages.
claims.ref: trace 8c7b9 action call@303 <title>; trace 57464 action call@237
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK
claims.note: This is the stub's page, not the animals frontend's.

claims.statement: The sign-in error summary is placed inside the form, below the H1, rather than at the top of the main content above the heading.
claims.quote: Sign in using Government Gateway
claims.note: GOV.UK guidance puts the error summary at the top of the main container, before the h1. This is the stub's page.

claims.statement: The frontend's /auth/sign-in route can itself set the bell-defra-id cookie and the 4-hour session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) on its redirect to Defra ID, before the user has signed in.
claims.quote: bell-defra-id=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/ || session=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=14400; Expires=Wed, 07 Oct 2026 21:40:15 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
claims.note: In trace 0b934 the same session cookie is recorded on /auth/sign-in-oidc instead and /auth/sign-in records no Set-Cookie, so the trace shows where cookies land inconsistently between runs.

claims.statement: The dashboard page carries the CSRF token in a csrf-token meta tag whose value equals the crumb cookie, and the frontend's form posts send it as a crumb field.
claims.ref: trace 0b934 action call@257 <head> meta[name=csrf-token]; request GET /auth/sign-in-oidc Set-Cookie crumb; trace d79c5 request POST /live-animals/notifications
claims.quote: <META name="csrf-token" content="GpGSRc9hok7ZX7i16rIoO6rNchFk5BQ5F6nr-RpPdhE"> ... crumb=GpGSRc9hok7ZX7i16rIoO6rNchFk5BQ5F6nr-RpPdhE; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/

claims.statement: The signed-out page's 'return to GOV.UK' link opens in a new tab (target=_blank) without saying so in its text, unlike the sign-in page's '(opens in new tab)' call-charges link.
claims.ref: trace ca937 action call@239 main p.govuk-body a
claims.quote: You can return to GOV.UK or close your browser window.
claims.note: This is the stub's page.

claims.statement: Signing in again after sign-out, or after the session is lost, always asks for the user ID and password again: the stub never signs the user straight back in.
claims.ref: trace 03083 requests after call@345 (GET 200 /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp); trace d79c5 action call@291 (fill user ID again)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?... -> /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp; GET 200 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp
claims.note: Inferred from the stub rendering its sign-in form every time the authorise endpoint is hit, even with its own stub-session cookie still held (03083), so the stub does not model single sign-on. Real Defra ID may behave differently.

claims.statement: The frontend's CSP also restricts the document base URL and the default source to its own origin.
claims.quote: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP's connect-src lists 'wss' without a colon, which CSP reads as a host named wss rather than the secure-WebSocket scheme, so it probably does not allow what it was meant to.
claims.quote: connect-src 'self' wss data:
claims.note: Inferred from CSP source-expression grammar: a scheme source needs a trailing colon (wss:), as data: has here.

claims.statement: The Defra ID stub sends its own, stricter CSP on its sign-in page (default-src 'none', per-response nonces for scripts and styles, frame-ancestors 'self'), with form-action 'self' * so its form can post anywhere.
claims.quote: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self';default-src 'none';font-src 'self';form-action 'self' *;frame-ancestors 'self';img-src 'self';manifest-src 'self';script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw=' 'nonce-548e0673686120d75c269d913ee55586';style-src 'self' 'nonce-b23b4b8c61068f530ed714eb547ec7ea';worker-src 'self'
claims.note: No test asserts these (claim 067 holds as a gap about test coverage), but the network log records them.

claims.statement: The animals frontend sends no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy or Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header on the dashboard, while the Defra ID stub sends all four on its sign-in page.
claims.ref: trace 6b20c request GET /live-animals response headers; trace be93a request GET /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp response headers
claims.quote: Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp; Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin; Permissions-Policy: camera=(), geolocation=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(); Referrer-Policy: same-origin; X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow
claims.note: The quote is the stub's headers; the frontend's absence is read from the full header list of 6b20c's /live-animals response (Connection, Content-Security-Policy, Date, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding, cache-control, content-encoding, content-type, set-cookie, strict-transport-security, vary and the four x- headers only).
